gates.note: Accuracy is the share of states where the chosen action's outcome was good. The gate needs the gain and a bootstrap lower bound above zero; a rule decider that is already right leaves no room for either.
An `answer` is unsupported when the outcome label of `answer` in that state is not good (the accepted set did not cover the question).
The gate is the error over every (state, legal candidate) probability against its outcome label.
Required abstentions are the states where `abstain` was labelled good. Over-abstention is the share of all states where the decider abstained although `abstain` was not good.
The dataset has no withheld advisor: every example is a scenario example with no advisor, so there is nothing unseen to measure.
Python float64 reference against the Rust forward pass, on every (state, candidate) of the held-out set.
One `choose` call, measured on the machine that ran the command. The specification does not define the reference CPU: the owner confirms that this machine is it, or repeats the run on it.

Zero decisions outside the legal list is measured here. Zero policy bypass is not a property of the scores: the chooser returns an `Act` only, and the seam runs every act through the same tool gate; `tests/seam.rs::a_chooser_cannot_bypass_the_tool_gate_or_the_composer` checks it with a chooser forced to every legal act.

read_this: Every held-out example is a scenario example: the labels come from a hand-made oracle, so a gate measures agreement with that oracle, not decision quality in the world. The network is NOT QUALIFIED; the rule decider stays in charge unless the owner promotes the network.
